title: Tea From Both Hands
logline: A shopkeeper has given the same regular customer something small every day for years, more on some days and less on others, and neither of them has ever said why.
human_question: When the same person gives you the same kind of thing every day, what actually changes from one day to the next?

situation.what_happens: A shopkeeper and a long-standing customer meet almost every day over a counter. Something small is always given, and it is never quite the same: more on a good day, less on a bad one, sometimes with a word and sometimes without. Neither of them treats it as charity and neither has ever named it. Watched over several weeks, the variation becomes visible even though the transaction looks identical each morning.
situation.who_is_involved: A shopkeeper who has run the same counter for a long time; a regular customer who has been coming for years; other customers whose presence changes what can be said aloud.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the customer, dignity: being a person in a relationship rather than a case of need. For the shopkeeper, a private arrangement becoming public. For the viewer, whether repetition empties an act or quietly keeps it alive.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Arrangements like this usually start without being decided and continue without being discussed. They are pressured by money, by illness, by the arrival of anyone who might comment on them, and by the awkwardness of being asked about them. They end when one party moves, stops trading or dies. Reality decides whether either person will say anything about it at all, and whether being watched changes what is given.

concept_merge.why_together: C011 is the concept that grades the same good act by what is inside it, and its own example is one giver and one receiver on two different days. C019 explains why the days differ at all: the ordinary capacities that carry the act are reassembled each time and take the colour of that moment. Together they turn a transaction that looks unchanging into a sequence of distinct moments.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the unit the tradition cares about is the moment, not the habit; a relationship of years is made of mornings that are not equivalent to one another.

concept_links.why: The Margaya's own illustration is one giver, one recipient and the same kind of mind on different days, where the strength of intention differs between a coin and a note [C011-M:L26]. The digest warns that this is a comparison within one giver, never a ranking of rich and poor givers.

Ordinary capacities such as attention and effort are neither good nor bad in themselves and take the quality of the mind they serve, which is why a daily act is never quite identical [C019-P:L61-L63; C019-P:L49].

what_the_viewer_could_understand: An act repeated for years is not one long act: the texts measure goodness by the moment, and the same small gift carries a different weight of intention on different days.
what_must_be_real: The two people's actual relationship and their own reasons for it. The recipient must be a full, consenting participant, never a stand-in for need, and nothing may be given because a film is present.
position_hint: middle: the observation only works once repetition has already been established, so it sits after an opening rather than at one.
risks: Exposing the recipient's hardship for the camera
Turning a private, long-standing relationship into a demonstration
Implying that the size of a gift measures the giver's worth, which the source does not claim
drop_if: The recipient does not want to be filmed
The relationship turns out to be arranged rather than long-standing

connections.note: Its substance now lives inside IDEA-0093 as the repeat-recipient strand: the same giver and receiver, and the variation from one day to the next.

selection.reason: Same concepts and the same human act as IDEA-0093; its distinctive observation, day-to-day variation toward a recipient who returns, is stronger inside that film than as a second giving film.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
